current_prompt.body:
COMPUTE the probability that, when a unit-length stick is broken at two points chosen uniformly and independently at random, the ratio of the shortest piece (L_min) to the longest piece (L_max) is greater than or equal to 1/4.
RETURN the probability value.

current_plan.body:
DEFINE two independent uniform random variables X and Y on the interval [0,1] representing the break points.
ORDER the break points so that X ≤ Y.
COMPUTE the three segment lengths L1 = X, L2 = Y – X, L3 = 1 – Y.
IDENTIFY L_min as the smallest of {L1, L2, L3} and L_max as the largest of {L1, L2, L3}.
FORMULATE the condition C: L_min / L_max ≥ 1/4.
DETERMINE the region in the (X, Y) unit square where condition C holds.
SET UP the double integral of the joint density (constant 2) over the region satisfying C.
COMPUTE the probability by evaluating the integral.
PREPARE a detailed step-by-step derivation, including geometric interpretation of the region, integration limits, and algebraic simplifications.
RETURN the probability value as the final result.
